simple.summary: זֵד (zêd) means arrogant First listed occurrence: Isa 13 11.

definitions.full: H2086. zed זֵד adjective insolent, presumptuous : — ׳ז Prov 21:24 ; plural זֵדִים Jer 43:2 11 t.; — always masculine, and always of opposition to ׳י , wickedness; with qualified noun expressed, only הַזֵּדִים הָאֲנָשִׁים 43:2 , of opponents of Jeremiah; elsewhere used substantively, as technical term for godless, rebellious men; once singular שְׁמוֺ לֵץ יָהִיר זֵד Prov 21:24 a haughty insolent one, scorner is his name (|| זָדוֺן בְּעֶבְרַת עוֺשֶׂה ); usually plural Isa 13:11 ( ז ׳גְּאוֺן ; || עָרִיצִים גַּאֲוַת ); Mal 3:13 (|| רִשְׁעָה עשֵֹׁי ), Malachi 4:19 (|| עשֵֹׁה רִשְׁעָה ); and in Psa 86:14 (|| עָרִיצִים ), 119:21 (|| הַשֹּׁגִים מִמִּצְוֺתֶיךָ ), 119:51 ; 119:69 ; 119:78 ; 119:85 ; 119:122 ; so probably also 19:14 עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ חֲשׂךְ מִזֵּדִים גַּם also from presumptuous men hold back thy servant (Ew Ol Hup Che RVm); > presumptuous sins Deal. (AV RV).
